title: ECG for children
what: A nurse records your child's heart activity with sticky pads called electrodes. It is quick, safe, and painless.
why: At a routine checkup, before sports, kindergarten, or school, or for a heart murmur, fainting, or a racing heart.
duration: usually 5 to 10 minutes; the report is often ready the same day
tell_doctor: What bothers your child, if anything
If heart problems run in the family

prepare.title: Prep
prepare.text: None needed. Your child can eat and drink.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Comfortable clothes, so the chest, forearms, and lower legs are easy to uncover.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Do not put cream on the chest on the day of the ECG.

prepare.title: Mindset
prepare.text: Tell your child: the stickers will feel cold, but it will not hurt.

bring: Past ECGs, if you have them
A toy, to distract your child
steps: Your child lies on the couch, and you stay close
Suction cups or stickers are put on the arms, legs, and chest
Your child is asked to lie still and not talk
feel: Cold stickers. It does not hurt
Babies sometimes cry, and the recording is repeated once they calm down
after: You can go back to your usual day right away
The doctor's report is usually ready the same day
Go over the results with your pediatrician

faq.q: Why does a child's ECG look different from an adult's?
faq.a: Children have different normal values. The pulse is faster, and much that is unusual in adults is normal for a child.

faq.q: If my child cries, will the recording be ruined?
faq.a: It might. Then they wait until your child calms down and record again.

reminders.text: Your child's ECG is tomorrow. No prep needed. Dress your child comfortably and do not put cream on the chest.
